board.text: The electrical pressure that pushes charge through a circuit, measured in volts.
The rate of flow of charge, measured in amperes.
Students often think current gets "used up" as it flows around a circuit
board.justification: The SAME current returns to the source, because charge is conserved. It is ENERGY that gets delivered.

beats.narration: More pressure, more flow. Tighter pipe, less flow. Electricity works exactly the same way!

board.text: The opposition a material offers to the flow of current, measured in ohms (Ω).
Example: A bulb's thin tungsten filament has HIGH resistance - the struggle makes it glow.
Non-example: A thick copper wire has almost NO resistance - it stays cool and simply carries the flow.
Rule of thumb: thin, long and hot means MORE resistance; thick, short and cool means LESS.

quiz.question: A circuit runs on a 12 V battery. We swap it for a 24 V battery, keeping the same resistance. What happens to the current?
feedback_wrong: Tempting - but current depends directly on voltage. Change the push, and the flow must change.
That is the inverse trap! Halving happens when RESISTANCE doubles - not voltage.
Current is never used up - that is the classic misconception. Charge always returns to the source.
quiz.explanation: Ohm's Law says I = V / R. Doubling V while R stays constant exactly doubles I.

scenes.title: WORKED EXAMPLE - THE CEILING FAN
scenes.subtitle: From supply to current, step by step

board.text: A ceiling fan runs on a 230 V supply and has a resistance of 115 Ω. Find the current.
Step 1: Choose the form I = V / R
board.justification: Because we want the flow, from a known push and opposition.

board.text: Step 2: Substitute the values - I = 230 / 115, keeping volts and ohms consistent.
Step 3: Solve - I = 2 amperes flowing through the fan.

board.text: Every appliance in your home is a live Ohm's Law calculation.
Engineers size every wire, fuse and breaker in the grid using this one rule.
Tamil Nadu's grid delivers thousands of megawatts every day - and every single ampere of it is routed by V = IR.
